sentences.en: From The New York Times, I'm Natalie Kittroweff.
sentences.zh: 我是娜塔莉·基特罗夫，来自《纽约时报》。

sentences.en: This is The Daily.

sentences.en: Just as America is beginning to wrap its arms around the fentanyl crisis, a new kind of drug epidemic is emerging.
sentences.zh: 正当美国开始着手应对芬太尼危机之际，一种新型的毒品流行病正在浮现。

sentences.en: It's faster, more addictive, and far more lethal.
sentences.zh: 它作用更快、更易上瘾，也远为致命。

sentences.en: And what's driving it are new types of synthetic drugs, substances that can be made almost anywhere, altered endlessly, trafficked easily,
sentences.zh: 而推动这一切的是新型合成毒品——这些物质几乎在任何地方都能制造、能被无休止地改造、易于走私，

sentences.en: and then consumed in just about any form imaginable.
sentences.zh: 然后以你能想象到的几乎任何形式被消费。

sentences.en: Today, my colleague Azam Ahmed explains how these deadlier drugs are beginning to take hold and brings us inside one effort to do something about it.
sentences.zh: 今天，我的同事阿扎姆·艾哈迈德将解释这些更致命的毒品如何开始站稳脚跟，并带我们深入了解一项旨在解决这一问题的行动。

sentences.en: It's Tuesday.
sentences.zh: 今天是星期二。

sentences.en: May 26th.
Azam, welcome to The Daily.
sentences.zh: 阿扎姆，欢迎来到《每日新闻》。

sentences.en: It's wonderful to have you here in New York.
sentences.zh: 很高兴你能来纽约。

sentences.en: Well, thank you for having me.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你邀请我来。

sentences.en: You are here not only because you have won multiple awards for your investigations.
sentences.zh: 你来到这里，不仅因为你的调查报道曾多次获奖。

sentences.en: This is true.
sentences.zh: 这倒是真的。

sentences.en: You can't deny it.
sentences.zh: 你无法否认这一点。

sentences.en: Not only because you are, I think it's fair to say, a foreign correspondent's foreign correspondent, but because you are in the middle of truly mind-blowing
sentences.zh: 不仅因为你是——我想这么说很公平——外派记者中的外派记者，还因为你正身处真正令人匪夷所思的报导中心，

sentences.en: reporting on the new world of synthetic drugs.
sentences.zh: 也就是关于合成毒品新世界的报道。

sentences.en: And I think this is something that none of us, even me, who, you know, I have a special interest reporting experiences in this world,
sentences.zh: 而且我认为，这是我们所有人——甚至包括我，你知道的，我在这个领域有专门的报导兴趣和经验——

sentences.en: really understood until you started to break these stories.
sentences.zh: 在你看透并打破这些黑幕之前，都从未真正理解的。

sentences.en: So, I want to just start with how you got to this.
sentences.zh: 所以，我想先从你是如何接触到这个话题开始聊起。

sentences.en: What drew you in to these stories?
sentences.zh: 是什么吸引你关注这些故事的？

sentences.en: You know, obviously we work together in Mexico, and in Mexico you're constantly looking at the repercussions of the war on drugs.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，显然我们在墨西哥共事过，在墨西哥，你无时无刻不在直面禁毒战争带来的恶果。

sentences.en: You're looking at countless lives loSt.
sentences.zh: 你看到无数的生命消逝。

sentences.en: You're looking at, you know, inordinate amounts of drugs, fentanyl, moving north into the United States.
sentences.zh: 你看到，你知道的，数量惊人的毒品——芬太尼，正源源不断地向北流入美国。

sentences.en: You kind of see the mechanism of failure up close.
sentences.zh: 你近距离目睹了这种体制的失灵。

sentences.en: And we all know the war on drugs has failed.
sentences.zh: 我们都知道禁毒战争已经失败了。

sentences.en: We also know, like, it not only failed, it kind of made things worse.
sentences.zh: 我们也知道，它不仅失败了，而且还把事情弄得更糟了。

sentences.en: And you realize fentanyl, meth, two of the first sort of synthetic drugs were out there.
sentences.zh: 然后你意识到，芬太尼和甲基安非他命这两种最早的合成毒品已经出现。

sentences.en: Basically, they were harbingers of this sort of dystopian future that is upon us.
sentences.zh: 基本上，它们就是摆在我们面前的这种反乌托邦未来的预兆。

sentences.en: For most of human history, drugs have been grown in the land.
sentences.zh: 在人类历史的大部分时间里，毒品都是从大自然中种植出来的。

sentences.en: You know, when the war on drugs was first declared by President Nixon, there was cocaine, marijuana, heroin.
sentences.zh: 你知道，当尼克松总统首次宣战禁毒时，当时只有古柯碱、大麻、海洛因。

sentences.en: Yeah, the big ones.
sentences.zh: 对，就是那几种大宗毒品。

sentences.en: Now there's like 1,450 new psychoactive substances.
sentences.zh: 现在大约有1,450种新型精神活性物质。

sentences.en: These are novel.
sentences.zh: 这些都是前所未有的新东西。

sentences.en: Is that a real step?
sentences.zh: 这是一个真正的转折点吗？

sentences.en: That's a real step.
sentences.zh: 这绝对是个真正的转折点。

sentences.en: Yikes.
sentences.zh: 天哪。

sentences.en: It's gone up like, it's tripled in the last decade.
sentences.zh: 它增长了，比如说，在过去十年里翻了三番。

sentences.en: That's insane.
sentences.zh: 这太疯狂了。

sentences.en: I mean, the number of new drugs that are coming out, it's like chefs testing new recipes because it's all synthetic now.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，新涌现的毒品数量，就像厨师在测试新食谱一样，因为现在全都是合成的。

sentences.en: It's made in labs and you can basically turn a molecule and change it in all these different ways and have a completely new drug,
sentences.zh: 它们是在实验室里制造的，你基本上只要转动一个分子，以各种不同方式对其进行改造，就能得到一种全新的毒品，

sentences.en: which basically leads to the major point that they are largely more potent, more deadly, easier to manufacture, easier to smuggle, harder to track, harder to treat,
sentences.zh: 这基本上引出了最重要的一点：它们在很大程度上比人类历史上的几乎任何时候都更强效、更致命、更容易制造、更容易走私、更难追踪、更难治疗，

sentences.en: and more profitable than almost any time in human history.
sentences.zh: 并且利润也更高。

sentences.en: What you're describing is the kind of beginning of something, but that beginning is really important.
sentences.zh: 你所描述的是某种事物的开端，而这个开端极其重要。

sentences.en: This idea that you get a drug like fentanyl,
sentences.zh: 就是像芬太尼这样的毒品，

sentences.en: 50 times more powerful, I think, than heroin.
sentences.zh: 我想，它的药效是海洛因的50倍。

sentences.en: It's really compact.
sentences.zh: 它非常小巧。

sentences.en: It's really easy to transport.
sentences.zh: 非常便于运输。

sentences.en: It's really easy to make.
sentences.zh: 非常容易制造。

sentences.en: You can make it, I saw, in a kitchen in Sinaloa.
sentences.zh: 我亲眼看到，在锡那罗亚的一间厨房里就能做出来。

sentences.en: Randomly, you can open a lab anywhere.
sentences.zh: 随随便便，你在任何地方都能开个实验室。

sentences.en: There is a kind of revolution that happens with that first step.
sentences.zh: 伴随着这第一步，一场革命爆发了。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 完全正确。

sentences.en: And I think for good reason, we in the United States look at fentanyl as almost the end-all, be-all because of how many, I mean, these, like, massive numbers of death.
sentences.zh: 而且我认为，出于充分的理由，我们美国人把芬太尼视作终极威胁，因为它的死亡人数实在是太庞大了。

sentences.en: Like, we're not accustomed to that.
sentences.zh: 比如，我们对此很不习惯。

sentences.en: It's so pervasive, and yet there are now new drugs, much more powerful than fentanyl, that are popping up, not just in the United States, but all over the world.
sentences.zh: 它是如此无孔不入，然而现在，比芬太尼更强效的新型毒品正在不断涌现，不仅是在美国，而且遍布全世界。

sentences.en: Okay, talk about that.
sentences.zh: 好的，聊聊这个吧。

sentences.en: I want to hear about that.
sentences.zh: 我很想听听这方面的内幕。

sentences.en: So a drug called nitazines can be 20 to 40 times more potent than fentanyl.
sentences.zh: 有一种叫做尼秦类（nitazines）的毒品，其药效可能是芬太尼的20到40倍。

sentences.en: They're an opioid that was created in the 1950s by a Swiss pharmaceutical, but turned out to be so potent that it didn't really have a natural market.
sentences.zh: 它们是一种阿片类药物，由一家瑞士制药公司在20世纪50年代合成，但结果发现药效太强，以至于在现实中根本没有自然的市售需求。

sentences.en: And so it never went to market.
sentences.zh: 所以它从未真正上市。

sentences.en: And then somebody, basically, as this sort of fentanyl crisis was unfolding, mined some archive and found the formula for making nitazines, and they started producing it.
sentences.zh: 然后有人，基本上是在这场芬太尼危机爆发的同时，翻阅了一些历史档案，找到了制造尼秦类的配方，并开始生产它。

sentences.en: Once they started producing it, they now have like a dozen different variants of nitazines that have been discovered all over the place.
sentences.zh: 一旦他们开始生产，现在他们就已经研发出了十几种不同变体的尼秦类毒品，这些毒品在各地都被发现了。

sentences.en: You're finding them in the United States.
sentences.zh: 你在美国能找到它们。

sentences.en: You're finding them throughout Europe.
sentences.zh: 你在全欧洲也能找到它们。

sentences.en: And one of the reasons you're finding them in Europe is because fentanyl has been so controlled and so tightly managed.
sentences.zh: 你在欧洲能找到它们的原因之一，就是因为芬太尼受到的管制和监控太严格了。

sentences.en: And this is important because this is the heart and center of why the drug war kind of made everything worse.
sentences.zh: 这一点很重要，因为这正是禁毒战争把一切弄得更糟的核心与关键所在。

sentences.en: So you're like, shit, we got to do something about fentanyl.
sentences.zh: 所以你会想，靠，我们得对芬太尼做点什么。

sentences.en: This is killing way too many people.
sentences.zh: 这玩艺儿害死的人实在太多了。

sentences.en: Let's control the precursor chemicals.
sentences.zh: 让我们控制前体化学品吧。

sentences.en: Let's pressure Chinese pharma for making this stuff.
sentences.zh: 向制造这些东西的中国制药施压。

sentences.en: Let's crack down on the Mexican cartels.
sentences.zh: 严厉打击墨西哥贩毒集团。

sentences.en: Great.
sentences.zh: 太棒了。

sentences.en: This is the approach of the drug war.
sentences.zh: 这就是禁毒战争的方法论。

sentences.en: It's to focus on enforcement, to focus on supply.
sentences.zh: 它的重点在于执法，重点在于打击供应端。

sentences.en: Supply.
sentences.zh: 供应端。

sentences.en: To focus on the supply side.
sentences.zh: 把焦点放在供应端。

sentences.en: And then they're like, oh, cool.
sentences.zh: 然后他们就会想，哦，酷。

sentences.en: Okay, we'll just come up with something else.
sentences.zh: 好吧，那我们大不了就换个别的配方。

sentences.en: So now they've made nitazines available on the market.
sentences.zh: 于是现在他们把尼秦类毒品投放到市场上。

sentences.en: And that is gradually expanding and more people are dying from it.
sentences.zh: 而这正在逐渐扩大，越来越多的人因此丧命。

sentences.en: But now there's things that are even going to replace nitazines that are popping up in certain places.
sentences.zh: 但现在，甚至还有准备取代尼秦类的东西正在某些地方冒出来。

sentences.en: That is the thing about synthetic drugs.
sentences.zh: 这就是合成毒品的本质。

sentences.en: Basically, what you've described is the idea that regulation just breeds innovation.
sentences.zh: 基本上，你刚才描述的就是监管只会催生创新。

sentences.en: Innovation.
sentences.zh: 创新。

sentences.en: It's one of the most entrepreneurial markets in the world.
sentences.zh: 这是世界上最具创业精神的市场之一。

sentences.en: I mean, they find new ways because as long as you have demand, someone's going to figure out how to supply it because if it's restricted, it's going to be lucrative.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他们总能找到新方法，因为只要有需求，就会有人想方设法去供应，因为如果它被限制了，那它就会变得利润丰厚。

sentences.en: I mean, we're looking at a totally different universe.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我们正在面对一个完全不同的宇宙。

sentences.en: Okay, so now I want to talk about your latest investigation that recently came out that talks about the Cook County Jail in Chicago.
sentences.zh: 好的，现在我想谈谈你最近刚发表的最新调查报道，其中讲到了芝加哥的库克县监狱。

sentences.en: Because while these drugs might not be on every street corner yet, you have found that the place that they're almost being incubated is in American jails and prisons.
sentences.zh: 因为虽然这些毒品可能还没出现在每一个街角，但你发现它们几乎正在美国的看守所和监狱里被孵化。

sentences.en: So walk me through what you found in Cook County.
sentences.zh: 所以，请带我了解一下你在库克县的发现。

sentences.en: Walk me through that story.
sentences.zh: 带我梳理一下那个故事。

sentences.en: So in January 2023, jail authorities are called to the scene of a dead body and they show up
sentences.zh: 所以在2023年1月，监狱官方接到报告赶到一处出现死者的现场，当他们到达时，

sentences.en: and there's this inmate who basically has died from some kind of a overdose, but they can't find anything.
sentences.zh: 发现这名囚犯基本上是因为某种过量吸毒而死，但他们却找不到任何东西。

sentences.en: There's no contraband.
sentences.zh: 没有违禁品。

sentences.en: They just find all these little paper roaches sort of scattered around like burned confetti.
sentences.zh: 他们只发现周围散落着一堆小纸片，就像烧焦的五彩纸屑一样。

sentences.en: And they're kind of mystified by what this is, but it's clear the guy's overdosed.
sentences.zh: 他们对这东西感到有些困惑，但很显然这人是吸毒过量了。

sentences.en: And it sort of launches them on this incredible odyssey where they start having these deaths
sentences.zh: 而这也让他们开启了一场不可思议的探索之旅，因为随后他们不断遭遇这样的死亡事件

sentences.en: and these crazy overdoses, people going into almost these exorcistic fits, having seizures.
sentences.zh: 和疯狂的吸毒过量案例，人们几乎陷入驱魔般的抽搐，并开始癫痫发作。

sentences.en: And they're watching them on camera and then it clicks.
sentences.zh: 他们通过监控看着这一切，然后突然恍然大悟。

sentences.en: They're like, oh my God, they're smoking paper.
sentences.zh: 他们说，哦天哪，他们在抽纸。

sentences.en: They're literally smoking paper.
sentences.zh: 他们字面意义上是在抽纸。

sentences.en: And they realize what's happened is someone has figured out how to turn synthetic drugs into liquid, soak sheets of paper into it, and then smuggle paper into the jail.
sentences.zh: 并且他们意识到发生的事情是：有人想出了如何把合成毒品变成液体，浸泡纸张，然后把纸走私进监狱里。

sentences.en: Now, paper is the most ubiquitous thing in the world, right?
sentences.zh: 现在，纸是世界上最无处不在的东西，对吧？

sentences.en: It's been around since ancient Egypt.
sentences.zh: 它自古埃及以来就存在了。

sentences.en: How do you stop paper?
sentences.zh: 你该怎么拦截纸张？

sentences.en: Well, so just to back up, what is on this paper?
sentences.zh: 好吧，那么先退一步说，这纸上到底有什么？

sentences.en: Like, do they know?
sentences.zh: 诸如，他们知道吗？

sentences.en: You're describing the exorcistic fit and I'm wondering what causes that.
sentences.zh: 你刚才描述了那种驱魔般的抽搐，我很好奇是什么引发了那种反应。

sentences.en: At the time, they don't know what's on it.
sentences.zh: 当时，他们并不知道上面有什么。

sentences.en: They would find someone high or maybe find someone dead.
sentences.zh: 他们会发现某人嗨高了，或者发现某人死了。

sentences.en: They would get a toxicology report of the person who died to figure out what they might have smoked.
sentences.zh: 他们会获取死者的毒理学报告，以弄清楚他们可能吸了什么。

sentences.en: They would also find paper within the jail facility itself and they'd send that off to get tested.
sentences.zh: 他们还会在监狱内部找到纸张，并将其送去检测。

sentences.en: It would be anything from like cannabinoids, which is a synthetic form of cannabis, which
sentences.zh: 检测结果从大麻素——一种大麻的合成形式，

sentences.en: can actually be deadly, to sometimes fentanyl, like all different kinds of synthetic substances.
sentences.zh: 实际上可能是致命的——到有时甚至是芬太尼，各种各样的合成物质应有尽有。

sentences.en: I mean, at some point, they were finding recipes for raid and rat poison.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，在某个时候，他们甚至在配方里发现了雷达（杀虫剂）和老鼠药。

sentences.en: And then in August of 2024, they found this single sheet of paper that had 10 different synthetic drugs on it, which didn't make any sense, right?
sentences.zh: 然后在2024年8月，他们发现了一张单独的纸，上面竟然含有10种不同的合成毒品，这根本说不通，对吧？

sentences.en: Because it was all different sorts of things that have different corporal implications, right?
sentences.zh: 因为这全都是些具有不同生理影响的杂七杂八的东西，对吧？

sentences.en: Like it was cannabinoids, it was opioids, like they affect you.
sentences.zh: 就像大麻素、阿片类药物，它们会影响你。

sentences.en: The high is different.
sentences.zh: 嗨的感觉是不同的。

sentences.en: Is it 10 different substances all in different quadrants?
sentences.zh: 这10种不同的物质全部分布在不同的象限里吗？

sentences.en: No, they're overlapping.
sentences.zh: 不，它们是相互重叠的。

sentences.en: It basically, the best we could figure is somebody had a bunch of chemicals they were spraying on paper and they just wanted to get rid of them all.
sentences.zh: 基本上，我们能想到的最佳解释是，某人手里有一堆化学品，他们正把它们喷洒在纸上，然后他们只想把这些东西统统处理掉。

sentences.en: So they dumped them all on one sheet and that went in.
sentences.zh: 所以他们把所有的东西都倒在了一张纸上，然后那张纸就被带进去了。

sentences.en: I mean, from your reporting on fentanyl, there's not really a calculation of how deadly this could be, how potent this is going to be.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，从你对芬太尼的报道来看，人们根本无法计算这东西到底能有多致命，它的药效究竟会有多强。

sentences.en: To the extent that there's a calculation, the calculation is how bad can we make this?
sentences.zh: 如果说有什么计算的话，那就是：我们能把这东西搞得有多烂（多极端）？

sentences.en: Meaning how potent, how strong?
sentences.zh: 意思是多强效，多大劲？

sentences.en: Completely.
sentences.zh: 完全正确。

sentences.en: That's exactly right.
sentences.zh: 正是如此。

sentences.en: It's the more potent, the less I have to smuggle.

sentences.zh: 他被提审了。

sentences.en: And I go back to Cook County.
sentences.zh: 而我回到了库克县。

sentences.en: I'm like, wow.
sentences.zh: 当时我就想，哇。

sentences.en: You know, like a year later, here it is.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，大约一年后，事情就这样发生了。

sentences.en: You've busted like the biggest paper pusher in Illinois, presumably.
sentences.zh: 你们大概抓了伊利诺伊州最大的贩毒推手吧。

sentences.en: Like, what's going to happen?
sentences.zh: 就像是，接下来会发生什么？

sentences.en: And in my mind, I guess I already kind of knew.
sentences.zh: 而在我心里，我想我其实已经隐约知道了。

sentences.en: I was like, this isn't going to change anything.
sentences.zh: 我就觉得，这根本改变不了什么。

sentences.en: Like, it's every time we take down a kingpin, it ranges from like bad to worse, the response to it.
sentences.zh: 每次我们打掉一个毒枭，随之而来的反应从糟糕到更糟不等。

sentences.en: I mean, our time in Mexico.
sentences.zh: 我是说，我们在墨西哥的那段日子。

sentences.en: Every time they killed one of these capos, they like announced it with this sort of saber rattle of like, look, we did it again.
sentences.zh: 每当他们杀死其中一个贩毒集团头目，他们就会大肆宣扬，带着那种耀武扬威的姿态，仿佛在说：看，我们又办到了一次。

sentences.en: Every time, there would be a fight for control.
sentences.zh: 每一次，都会引发一场权力争夺战。

sentences.en: There would be more violence.
sentences.zh: 暴力事件会更多。

sentences.en: Worst case scenario, it would be the Hydra effect where they cut off the head and multiple heads sprung up.
sentences.zh: 最坏的情况是，会出现九头蛇效应——砍下一个头，又长出好几个头。

sentences.en: And then you just had disorganized chaos.
sentences.zh: 然后你面对的就只是一盘散沙般的混乱。

sentences.en: In the same way, they bust this guy, and I'm talking to Justin, the investigator, and he's like, did we solve a mystery today?
sentences.zh: 同样地，他们抓了这个人，我和调查员贾斯廷交谈，他问：我们今天破案了吗？

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Did we solve the mystery?
sentences.zh: 我们破案了吗？

sentences.en: Do I think this is going to change the phenomenon?
sentences.zh: 你认为这会改变这种现象吗？

sentences.en: He's like, no.
sentences.zh: 他说，不会。

sentences.en: So after all that, he basically recognizes, yeah, this is a win for us, but this is nowhere near the end.
sentences.zh: 所以在经历了这一切之后，他基本上意识到，是的，这对我们来说是一场胜利，但这离结束还远得很。

sentences.en: Doing this is not going to solve the problem.
sentences.zh: 这样做并不能解决问题。

sentences.en: This is another spoke in the turning wheel, you know?
sentences.zh: 这只是转动车轮上的又一根辐条，你知道吗？

sentences.en: So, I mean, did that pan out?
sentences.zh: 所以，我是说，情况真的如预料那样发展了吗？

sentences.en: It did.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: It did.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: A couple months later, I checked in on the data, and they were like, we're having the same number of overdoses.
sentences.zh: 几个月后，我查阅了数据，他们的反应是：我们的吸毒过量人数和以前一样多。

sentences.en: They now have something that's five times more potent on paper there.
sentences.zh: 而且从纸面上看，他们现在有了药效强上五倍的新东西。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: But also, around that time, they found new ways and novel ways in which they're getting the drugs in.
sentences.zh: 但与此同时，他们也找到了运毒的新途径和新方法。

sentences.en: People had figured out how to use Amazon to send drug-soaked paper into the jail.
sentences.zh: 人们已经摸清了如何利用亚马逊将浸透毒品的纸张寄进监狱。

sentences.en: Through Amazon.
sentences.zh: 通过亚马逊。

sentences.en: Through Amazon.
sentences.zh: 通过亚马逊。

sentences.en: Basically, someone would register as a third-party seller, would have a drug-soaked book listed on that, and then the person would buy from that direct seller,
sentences.zh: 基本上，某人会注册为第三方卖家，在上面挂出一本浸透毒品的书，然后买家直接从那个卖家那里购买，

sentences.en: thereby sort of laundering a drug-soaked book through Amazon and Amazon packaging, which made it incredibly difficult.
sentences.zh: 从而通过亚马逊及其包装将一本浸透毒品的书“洗白”，这让事情变得极其困难。

sentences.en: Because prior to that, jailhouse authorities were like, we don't have to worry about that.
sentences.zh: 因为在此之前，监狱当局的想法是：我们不用担心这个。

sentences.en: It's coming from Amazon.
sentences.zh: 这是从亚马逊买的。

sentences.en: That's crazy.
sentences.zh: 这太疯狂了。

sentences.en: What an image.
sentences.zh: 多贴切的画面啊。

sentences.en: It was just that representative microcosm of this quixotic game of whack-a-mole that they continue to play as they find new—like, we're going to crack down on that.
sentences.zh: 这恰恰是这种荒诞的“打地鼠”游戏的一个缩影——他们不断地发现新情况并继续玩下去，比如：我们要严厉打击那个。

sentences.en: Okay, they're going to do something else.
sentences.zh: 好吧，他们又会搞出别的东西。

sentences.en: We're going to crack down on this drug.
sentences.zh: 我们要严厉打击这种毒品。

sentences.en: Okay, we're going to get another drug.
sentences.zh: 好吧，我们又会弄到另一种毒品。

sentences.en: And this is in the most controlled setting you can imagine.
sentences.zh: 而这还是在你能想象到的最受控制的环境里。

sentences.en: Yeah, yeah.
sentences.zh: 对，对。

sentences.en: That, I think, is what scares them the most, because they're having a hard time controlling that in a jail setting.
sentences.zh: 我想，这才是最让他们害怕的地方，因为他们在监狱这样的环境下都很难控制住这些。

sentences.en: What happens when that hits the street?
sentences.zh: 当这些流入街头时会发生什么？

sentences.en: Okay, so now that you have your arms kind of wrapped around just how bad this new synthetic drug epidemic really is,
sentences.zh: 好了，既然你已经大致了解了这场新型合成毒品疫情究竟有多严重，

sentences.en: just how much invention and reinvention is kind of built into it, I want to ask, and I want to turn to the question of, what do we do now?
sentences.zh: 也了解了其中蕴含了多少发明与推陈出新，我想问，我想把话题转向：我们现在该怎么办？

sentences.en: Because I think a lot of people who hear this and who have not spent more than a year covering it are going to be wondering, like, how do we stop this?
sentences.zh: 因为我想很多听到这些、且报道这一问题不超过一年的人都会在想，我们究竟该如何阻止这一切？

sentences.en: What is the path?
sentences.zh: 出路在哪里？

sentences.en: It's funny, you know, as journalists, we try to, like, kind of stick with, like, presenting what's happening, but you can't help but think about, what's the road that led us here?
sentences.zh: 说来也奇怪，你知道，作为记者，我们努力坚持呈现正在发生的事情，但你还是忍不住去想：是什么样的道路把我们带到了这里？

sentences.en: Is there a road to lead us out?
sentences.zh: 有没有一条路能引领我们走出去？

sentences.en: Or are we kind of trapped in this cyclical framework where we just keep doing more of the same thing?
sentences.zh: 还是说我们陷入了这种循环的框架中，只能不断重复同样的做法？

sentences.en: And that is the inescapable feeling, especially with this administration, which has opted to kick more ass, so to speak, against drug cartels and smuggling and all of that,
sentences.zh: 那种无法摆脱的感觉挥之不去，特别是本届政府选择对贩毒集团、走私及所有相关行当采取更严厉的打击手段时，

sentences.en: is that that hasn't worked.
sentences.zh: 结果却是这根本不管用。

sentences.en: You might see the Mexican police motivated to, like, bust an arco, but we've busted a lot of these guys before, and all it does is just a new kingpin emerges.
sentences.zh: 你可能会看到墨西哥警方出于积极性去抓捕一个毒贩，但我们以前已经抓过很多这样的人了，而这起到的唯一作用就是涌现出一个新的毒枭。

sentences.en: What about the other option, the alternate route here from the one that the drug war has taken, addressing demand?
sentences.zh: 那另一个选择呢？与毒品战争所走的路不同的另一条路线——解决需求问题？

sentences.en: Yeah, legalization or decriminalization.
sentences.zh: 对，合法化或非罪化。

sentences.en: Or any way of kind of, yes, of getting at the consumption side.
sentences.zh: 或者通过任何方式，是的，从消费端入手。

sentences.en: The fact that in Mexico,
sentences.zh: 事实上，在墨西哥，

sentences.en: the idea that you're going to stop drugs from being produced without dealing with the fact that the largest consumer market in the entire world sits right on top of this country,
sentences.zh: 如果认为只要不解决世界上最大消费市场就紧挨着这个国家、就在其边境上的现实，就能阻止毒品的生产，这简直是天大的笑话。

sentences.en: on its border, is sort of laughable.
sentences.zh: 在它的边境上，这简直有点可笑。

sentences.en: What about those methods?
sentences.zh: 那些方法呢？

sentences.en: How do you see that?
sentences.zh: 你是怎么看的？

sentences.en: Is that a potential way forward here?
sentences.zh: 这会是未来的潜在出路吗？

sentences.en: The thing that struck me is, like, this whole framework around legalization, decriminalization, we have been talking about it for so long.
sentences.zh: 让我感到震撼的是，围绕合法化和非罪化的整个框架，我们已经讨论了这么久。

sentences.en: There's a few countries that have done it, like Portugal, but by and large, experiments in this have been few and far between,
sentences.zh: 有一些国家已经这样做了，比如葡萄牙，但总的来说，这方面的实验寥寥无几，

sentences.en: and it's mostly just been a talking point among progressives.
sentences.zh: 而且它大多只是进步派的一个谈资。

sentences.en: The problem is,
sentences.zh: 问题在于，

sentences.en: it's too dangerous to kind of have a decriminalization procedure that creates a wider array of availability for things that chemists and scientists and doctors themselves don't know the human implications.
sentences.zh: 实行非罪化程序太危险了，它会为那些连化学家、科学家和医生自己都不知道其对人类影响的东西创造出更广泛的可获得性。

sentences.en: Like, nitazines has never been tested in a medical setting for any long period of time.
sentences.zh: 就像尼秦类药物从未在医疗环境中长期接受过测试一样。

sentences.en: We're still arguing about a paradigm that might have worked when there were just three or four drugs we were worried about.
sentences.zh: 我们还在争论一个范式，它可能在只有三四种令人担忧的毒品时管用。

sentences.en: Now we're worried about 1,400 and counting.
sentences.zh: 现在我们面对的是1400种而且还在增加的毒品。

sentences.en: So what you're talking about is a situation where, like, maybe decriminalization could have been a solution in before times, but we're not in before times.
sentences.zh: 所以你谈论的是这样一种情况：也许非罪化在过去可能是个解决方案，但我们已经回不到过去了。

sentences.en: The horse is out of the barn, basically.
sentences.zh: 基本上就是覆水难收了。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 正是如此。

sentences.en: That's exactly what I'm saying.
sentences.zh: 我就是这个意思。

sentences.en: So I think to answer your bigger question, which is, what do we do?
sentences.zh: 所以我想回答你的宏大问题，也就是：我们该怎么办？

sentences.en: If you talk to a lot of scientists, they'll be like, yeah, I don't think legalization is the way or decriminalization is the way to go either.
sentences.zh: 如果你和很多科学家谈谈，他们会觉得：是的，我也不认为合法化或非罪化是正确的出路。

sentences.en: You should have elements of this, like harm reduction, for instance.
sentences.zh: 你应该采用其中的某些元素，比如减少危害。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: That is an important component of this that Europe is really focused on.
sentences.zh: 这是欧洲非常重视的一个重要组成部分。

sentences.en: And harm reduction is basically what it sounds like.
sentences.zh: 减少危害基本上就如其字面意思那样。

sentences.en: We understand people are going to use drugs.
sentences.zh: 我们理解人们会吸毒。

sentences.en: We understand that we're never going to be able to fully reduce all of the demand.
sentences.zh: 我们理解我们永远无法完全消除所有的需求。

sentences.en: So how do we keep deaths and serious injury from happening?
sentences.zh: 那么我们该如何防止死亡和严重伤害的发生？

sentences.en: That's interesting.
sentences.zh: 这很有趣。

sentences.en: We swap needles, right?
sentences.zh: 我们交换针头，对吧？

sentences.en: So no one's sharing needles.
sentences.zh: 这样就没有人共用针头了。

sentences.en: HIV rates plummet.
sentences.zh: 艾滋病毒感染率急剧下降。

sentences.en: We issue Narcan everywhere so that if your friend overdoses, you give them a shot of Narcan, you revive them.
sentences.zh: 我们在各处发放纳洛酮，这样如果你的朋友吸毒过量，你就可以给他注射一针纳洛酮，让他苏醒过来。

sentences.en: They don't die.
sentences.zh: 他们就不会死。

sentences.en: We pass laws that are like, if you call the cops or rather the authorities because your friend is overdosed and you're worried they're going to die,
sentences.zh: 我们通过这样的法律：如果你因为朋友吸毒过量而担心他会死，因而报警或者联系当局，

sentences.en: we're not going to prosecute you or send you to jail.
sentences.zh: 我们不会起诉你，也不会把你送进监狱。

sentences.en: Because that then means fewer people will die.
sentences.zh: 因为这意味着更少的人会死亡。

sentences.en: It's treating it as a public health crisis and not a criminal problem.
sentences.zh: 这是把它当作一个公共卫生危机，而不是犯罪问题来对待。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Which is something the United States has always struggled with.
sentences.zh: 这也是美国一直以来感到棘手的地方。

sentences.en: It sounds like what you've learned is that we don't have the language to describe what we're seeing.
sentences.zh: 听起来你学到的经验是，我们缺乏描述当前所见事物的语言。

sentences.en: And so a first step is to just all of us wrap our minds around what this is and really change our entire framework of thinking about it.
sentences.zh: 所以第一步是让我们所有人共同理解这究竟是什么，并真正改变我们看待它的整个思维框架。

sentences.en: I think that's right.
sentences.zh: 我想是的。

sentences.en: I think it's also just looking at it with like dispassionate, brutal honesty.
sentences.zh: 我认为这也是在以冷静、残酷的诚实来审视它。

sentences.en: Which has always been hard for us.
sentences.zh: 而这对于我们来说一直都很难。

sentences.en: We are still thinking that blowing up boats or like targeting kingpins is going to stop this.
sentences.zh: 我们依然认为炸毁船只或者把目标对准毒枭就能阻止这一切。

sentences.en: And it's clearly not.
sentences.zh: 但显然并非如此。

sentences.en: You can have little bits of pressure and maybe that can even be a good thing to force the Mexicans to actually do something about this gigantic industry within their borders.
sentences.zh: 你可以施加一点压力，或许这甚至能成为一件好事，迫使墨西哥人真正采取行动来对付他们境内这个庞大的产业。

sentences.en: But that's not going to solve it.
sentences.zh: 但这并不能解决问题。

sentences.en: We've never needed more creative thinking about this problem because it's never been more dangerous or creative.
sentences.zh: 我们从未像现在这样需要对这个问题进行更多创造性的思考，因为它从未像现在这样危险或充满创意。

sentences.en: We're kind of moving in opposite directions on one of the most costly issues of our time.
sentences.zh: 我们在我们这个时代代价最高昂的问题之一上，正朝着相反的方向前进。

sentences.en: Thank you so much for being on the show.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢你作客本节目。

sentences.en: Thanks for having me.
sentences.zh: 谢谢邀请。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: Here's what else you need to know today.
sentences.zh: 以下是你今天还需要了解的其他新闻。

sentences.en: On Monday night, U.S.
sentences.zh: 周一晚间，美国

sentences.en: officials said that American forces had carried out new strikes on missile launch sites in Iran and on boats trying to place mines.
sentences.zh: 官员表示，美军对伊朗的导弹发射场以及试图放置水雷的船只实施了新的打击。

sentences.en: U.S.
sentences.zh: 美国

sentences.en: Central Command said the strikes were defensive and intended to protect U.S.
sentences.zh: 中央司令部表示，这些打击是防御性的，旨在保护美国

sentences.en: troops.
sentences.zh: 部队。

sentences.en: The strikes came hours after Iran's top negotiators arrived in Qatar for talks on a peace agreement with the U.S.
sentences.zh: 这些打击发生数小时前，伊朗的最高谈判代表刚抵达卡塔尔，准备与美国就和平协议进行会谈。

sentences.en: The terms of any potential deal remain unclear, though, including the fate of Iran's nuclear program, its missile stockpile,
sentences.zh: 然而，任何潜在协议的条款仍不明确，包括伊朗核计划的命运、其导弹库存，

sentences.en: and whether it would keep exerting control over the Strait of Hormuz.
sentences.zh: 以及它是否会继续对霍尔木兹海峡施加控制。

sentences.en: Israel also signaled on Monday that it intended to escalate fighting against Hezbollah in Lebanon, which could further complicate the talks.
sentences.zh: 以色列周一也发出信号，表示打算在黎巴嫩升级针对真主党的战斗，这可能会使会谈进一步复杂化。

sentences.en: Iran has said that any agreement to end the war with the U.S.
sentences.zh: 伊朗方面表示，任何旨在结束与美国

sentences.en: and Israel should also cover the Israeli conflict with Hezbollah.
sentences.zh: 及以色列战争的协议，都应涵盖以色列与真主党的冲突。

sentences.en: And a gunman was shot and killed by Secret Service officers on Saturday after he opened fire near the White House.
sentences.zh: 周六，一名枪手在白宫附近开枪后，被特勤局特工开枪击毙。

sentences.en: Trump was in the building at the time and had made it known that he would be spending the weekend there.
sentences.zh: 特朗普当时正在大楼内，并且已经公开表示他将在那里度过周末。

sentences.en: A bystander who was struck by gunfire was in stable condition on Sunday.
sentences.zh: 一名被流弹击中的旁观者在周日情况稳定。

sentences.en: Finally,
sentences.zh: 最后，

sentences.en: Artificial intelligence now demands to be disarmed, freed from logics that turn it into an instrument of domination, exclusion, and death.
sentences.zh: 人工智能现在要求被解除武装，从将其变成统治、排斥和死亡工具的逻辑中解放出来。

sentences.en: Pope Leo XIV delivered a stark warning to humanity on Monday about the risks of artificial intelligence.
sentences.zh: 教皇利奥十四世周临向人类发出严厉警告，谈到了人工智能的风险。

sentences.en: Decisions about technology must never be separated from conscience and responsibility.
sentences.zh: 关于技术的决定绝不能与良知和责任分离。

sentences.en: The message came in what's known as a papal encyclical, which is a centuries-old form of communication used by the Pope to deliver teachings on moral or social challenges.
sentences.zh: 这一信息是通过所谓的通谕发布的，这是教皇用来传授关于道德或社会挑战的教义的一种历经数百年历史的交流形式。

sentences.en: He specifically called for government regulation of the companies driving the AI boom, retraining for the workers threatened by it,
sentences.zh: 他特别呼吁对推动人工智能热潮的公司进行政府监管，为受其威胁的工人提供再培训，

sentences.en: and actions to shield children from hyper-sexualized or fake AI-generated information.
sentences.zh: 并采取行动保护儿童免受过度色情化或人工智能生成的虚假信息的影响。

sentences.en: For decades, the Brooklyn Democratic Party operated as a tightly controlled machine.
sentences.zh: 几十年来，布鲁克林民主党一直作为一个受到严密控制的机器在运作。

sentences.en: Until this summer.
sentences.zh: 直到今年夏天。

sentences.en: When elections ushered in a bunch of self-described reformers.
sentences.zh: 当时选举迎进来了一群自称改革派的人士。

sentences.en: Ever since, the party has been in the grip of a bruising, chaotic, and sometimes thrilling fight.
sentences.zh: 从那以后，该党就陷入了一场残酷、混乱且有时扣人心弦的权力斗争中。

sentences.en: In the latest episode of Metro, with me, Sarah Koenig, stories of people trying to maintain their influence and losing control along the way.
